observations.contract: File size belongs to the bytes actually read
observations.trace: Startup load_combat_config first calls metadata(path), rejects length zero or greater than64 KiB, then separately calls read_to_string(path), with no bounded read. TacticalSceneInput::load similarly checks metadata against32 MiB then separately calls fs::read(path) before JSON parsing and validation. If the path is replaced or its content grows between these operations, the observed metadata can be within the cap while the subsequent whole-file read consumes larger bytes; the cap is not enforced on that read.
observations.remaining: Conditional source reasoning; no file was modified, parser run, memory pressure observed or adversary demonstrated. The normal static oversized scene test is only source evidence and does not exercise that interleaving. A repair must bound bytes read from the opened input itself, reject over-limit content before parsing, and keep typed input/error ownership coordinated with the existing startup error finding.

observations.trace: The application registers the connected_players insert callback and a subscription on the readiness-triggered setup; its on_error callback logs only. Pinned SDK2.6.1 SubscriptionManager removes the failed query from its manager and invokes on_error. Its ParsedMessage::SubscriptionError branch returns Ok; on an otherwise healthy connection that branch alone does not propagate a frame_tick error. The selected setup has no re-subscription, fail-closed state or exit on this callback. A later joining player can remain LoadingPlayer if no connected row reaches the drained mailbox.
observations.remaining: This is conditional on an actual subscription error and absence of another lifecycle/timeout recovery; no subscription, SDK, client, server, query, network, database, callback, mission or player ran. Do not assume the network remains healthy, a row is delivered, or a particular player-visible outcome. Coordinate retry/fail-closed policy, subscriptions and strategic authorization with all consumers.

observations.trace: Application setup does not retain the returned handle. The pinned SDK subscribe operation queues a cloned handle and its manager registers another clone; the generated handle delegates explicit unsubscribe to the SDK. This is evidence against assuming the application statement alone immediately unsubscribes the query.
observations.remaining: The selected source establishes clone ownership and explicit unsubscribe but not actual application, callback ordering, transport behavior, crash recovery or every generated-code lifecycle. Do not infer successful subscription delivery from the clone.

observations.trace: Generated obstacle x/z are authored grid ordinals and server materialization multiplies by input spacing then offsets by the terrain half extent. Window compilation selects the first supported eligible closure and creates the hinge at closed centre minus tangent times half width; the server animates from that negative-tangent hinge. Both client and server interior grab checks use the replicated closed opening centre. The specific right-hinged gate offset does not automatically transfer to this negative-tangent window path.
observations.remaining: Only selected static paths inspected. Actual generated geometry, alternative closure shapes, animation, scene collision, actors and user-visible reach remain unvalidated; no window, renderer or physics ran.
